claim: The source contains 42 complete tumour/matched-non-tumour patient pairs.
Phase 1 retained all 42 pairs for primary analysis and identified 7 patient pairs for a whole-pair sensitivity cohort; its label-blind PCA used 3759 eligible variable features.
Phase 3 identified 614 internal paired-abundance candidates and 1827 internal detection-pattern candidates under its frozen no-imputation primary rules.
Phase 4 found 271 Reactome v86 pathways supported by both ranked enrichment and patient-level paired scoring.
Phase 4 did not accept a stable patient cluster and therefore does not claim molecular or clinical subtypes.
Phase 5 evaluated 9 leakage-controlled pipelines with 25 repeated grouped outer validations and found no defensible compact panel.
Phase 6 evaluates 24 no-imputation multiverse scenarios across normalization, cohort, completeness and estimator.
Exact leave-one-patient-out refitting was completed for all 42 patients; 583/614 abundance candidates and 1804/1827 detection candidates retained core support in at least 80% of omissions.
Across the Phase 6 pathway multiverse, 596/783 Reactome v86 pathways met the prespecified direction-agreement and leading-edge-overlap robustness thresholds.
The leading Phase 5 abundance elastic-net model has grouped leave-one-patient-out AUC 0.985, balanced accuracy 0.964, and pair-orientation accuracy 0.976.
The 200-run paired-label full nested-pipeline negative control gave empirical p=0.004975; the observed AUC (0.977) exceeded the largest permuted AUC (0.732).
The overlap between Phase 3 tiered candidates and stable Phase 5 ML features was 140, exceeding the maximum overlap (64) in 1,000 random feature-key permutations (empirical p=0.000999).
The frozen integration rules classify 165 features as high-priority internal candidates, without implying biomarker validity.
No output is an externally validated biomarker, clinical panel, diagnostic test, causal mechanism, population-prevalence estimate, or treatment recommendation.
